learning_outcomes.text: Understand the design of a documented object-oriented software system
Recognize design flaws or virtues in an existing implemented object-oriented system
Develop (i.e., design, implement, test) with adequacy and effectiveness an object-oriented software system

syllabus_topics: Revision of fundamental object oriented concepts.
Modeling techniques for object oriented software. UML modeling, Unified Process, Agile Modeling, UML Diagrams (class diagrams, sequence diagrams)
Methods for requirements engineering, analysis and design in the object oriented paradigm.
Fundamental design principles and design metrics.
Introduction to software testing and maintenance.
Implementation of a sizeable software project in phases.
teaching_methods: Use of projector and interactive board during lectures
Use of computer for demonstration of programming
Use of computers in laboratories for development and testing of programs
Announcement of assessment marks via the course website
Use of email and social media for information exchange and improved communication with students
assessment_rules: The final score is a weighted sum of the final exam (70%) and the project (30%). A possible bonus of 10% for the best project can be awarded. The exam includes questions of program development and testing, evaluated based on correctness and completeness. The project has a significant level of complexity and volume in terms of programming.
